references.text: Israel settled in Heshbon, which is mentioned as the city that was destroyed in verse 30.
Heshbon and Dibon are listed among the cities that the tribes of Reuben and Gad asked to receive as their inheritance.
Dibon was rebuilt by the children of Gad, showing the city's significance during the conquest.
Moses reminds the people of the victory over Sihon and the capture of Heshbon.
Heshbon and Dibon are mentioned as part of the inherited land given to the tribe of Reuben.
Isaiah prophesies about Moab's fall and mentions Dibon, the same city referred to in Israel's song of victory.
Heshbon is mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy concerning Moab's destruction.
Jeremiah prophesies about Dibon's fall, which connects to the historical conquest.
Dibon is mentioned again in Jeremiah's judgment against Moab.
Jeremiah quotes parts of this ancient song about Heshbon in his prophecy against Moab.
